_comment: REAL SHAPE, INVENTED STRING VALUES. The top-level key set AND the value shape of /api/organizations/{org}/usage as it came back on the owner's own account (dev-only values dump, 2026-09-10). Numbers and booleans are the real ones; every string value is invented, because every identifier in this payload is a string. Its job is twofold: pin `usageShapeLines` against the shape that actually exists, and pin the exact card the parsers build from it — 5-hour 25 %, 7-day (all models) 70 %, 7-day Fable 80 % from `limits[]` (not derived), and an Extra usage row of 9.62 with no cap and therefore no bar.
_comment_strings: Every string value long enough to carry it is tagged STRINGVALUE- and padded to the length the real value had, so a leak into a log line is unmissable. Four are shorter than the tag and use 'SV-' padded to the same known length instead (kind/group/severity, whose real values were withheld — nothing may ever branch on them). Two are the real values: `currency` (3 chars) and `display_name` (5 chars, the dashboard's own 'Fable'). Neither is an identifier, and the card's own row text is built from them.
_comment_opaque_keys: The three 24-character keys are from the same account's key dump (2026-09-10) and are kept although the values dump does not list them: they are the documented limit of log redaction — an unbroken 20+ character run has no separator to split on, so `log.ts` masks the whole line. Two are null like most of the payload; one is an object with no `utilization`, which is dropped as malformed and silently, so `onIgnored` still reports exactly one key: amber_ladder.
